skill.name: python-cli-patterns
skill.description: Reusable Python CLI patterns for Typer and Rich, covering commands, options, Rich output, configuration loading, tests, and a starter template.
skill.summary: Design modern Python command-line tools with Typer, Rich, configuration patterns, and testing examples.
skill.author: 0xDarkMatter

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown examples that mention environment variables, hidden XDG paths, database URLs, and code fences. No prompt injection or credential exfiltration intent was found in the reviewed source files. One semantic issue remains: a Typer query example executes raw SQL supplied as a CLI argument.

remediation.suggestion: Replace the free-form SQL command with named operations or parameterized queries. Mark any administrative query tool as trusted-only.
Add notes that passwords, API keys, and database URLs must not be printed, logged, or included in generated output.
Tell generated CLIs to display the resolved config path before creating files in home-directory config locations.

semantic_findings.title: Raw SQL Execution Example
semantic_findings.description: The Typer query example accepts a sql argument from the command line and passes it directly to the database execution method. Generated tools could expose arbitrary database reads or writes if copied into untrusted CLIs.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The source shows a command argument named sql passed directly to ctx.obj.db.execute. This is a clear unsafe pattern, even though the file is documentation.

content.value_statement: Teams need consistent Python command-line interfaces for options, output, configuration, and tests. This skill provides Typer and Rich patterns for practical, production-ready CLI design.
actual_capabilities: Scaffold Typer apps with commands, subcommands, callbacks, options, and arguments.
Apply Rich tables, panels, progress bars, markdown rendering, syntax highlighting, and live displays.
Model configuration with TOML files, environment variables, Pydantic settings, and XDG directories.
Add typed arguments, interactive prompts, async commands, and CliRunner tests.
Use the included CLI template as a starting structure for a Python command-line app.
limitations: It provides examples and templates; it does not install dependencies or run commands by itself.
Database examples are simplified and need access controls before production use.
Examples assume Python 3.10 or newer with Typer and Rich available.
It does not cover packaging, distribution, or shell completion deployment in depth.

use_cases.title: Create an internal administration CLI
use_cases.description: Use command groups, typed options, Rich tables, and local configuration to build admin tools with predictable behavior.

use_cases.title: Improve operational scripts
use_cases.description: Replace ad hoc scripts with tested Typer commands, progress indicators, and explicit configuration paths.

use_cases.title: Add a developer-facing project CLI
use_cases.description: Expose common project tasks through a polished CLI with validation, help text, and CliRunner tests.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic CLI
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a basic Typer CLI for a project named <name> with one command, typed options, clear help text, and simple errors.

prompt_templates.title: Add Rich Output
prompt_templates.prompt: Update this CLI plan to use Rich tables, progress feedback, panels, and readable error messages without changing the command behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Design Configuration
prompt_templates.prompt: Design configuration handling for this CLI using TOML, environment variables, explicit paths, and tests for configuration precedence.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor a Full CLI
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this CLI design and propose a Typer architecture with subcommands, layered configuration, Rich output, async handling, and CliRunner tests.

output_examples.input: Build a CLI that imports files and shows progress.
output_examples.output: A command structure with path validation, progress reporting, success messages, error handling, and test scenarios.

output_examples.input: Add configuration support to an existing Python script.
output_examples.output: A configuration plan with file defaults, environment overrides, command-line precedence, and visible config paths.

output_examples.input: Make terminal output easier to scan.
output_examples.output: A Rich output plan using tables for records, panels for summaries, and clear stderr errors.

best_practices: Validate paths and options before doing filesystem work.
Keep secrets in environment variables or local config files and avoid printing them.
Add CliRunner tests for valid commands, invalid input, and environment-driven configuration.
anti_patterns: Do not execute raw SQL from command-line input unless the tool is strictly trusted.
Do not write configuration into hidden home paths without showing the resolved path.
Do not mix business logic directly into command callbacks when it should be tested separately.

faq.question: Which Python CLI frameworks does this skill focus on?
faq.answer: It focuses on Typer for command structure and Rich for terminal output.

faq.question: Can it help create a complete CLI application?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes a starter template and examples for commands, configuration, output, and tests.

faq.question: Does it handle secrets safely?
faq.answer: It shows environment-based configuration. Generated CLIs should avoid logging passwords, tokens, or database URLs.

faq.question: Does it include testing guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes CliRunner examples for successful commands, invalid input, options, and environment variables.

faq.question: Is it ready for production use?
faq.answer: Use it as a starting point. Add project-specific validation, authorization, logging, and security review.

faq.question: Does the skill run external commands?
faq.answer: No. The source content is documentation and templates. An agent may write files only when the user asks.
